summary: The revision closes the process gaps I raised — the three-level comparison now covers all seven mandated dimensions, section 18 audits every .mjs individually including the nine quality/ scripts, a human-attention policy was added, and the sole helper became conditional behind an admission test with an explicit statement that vNext stays at level 1 if direct CLI suffices. Its 'Replace, do not retain' verdict for model-set/project-key/safe-fs is a genuine precision that prevents coupling returning through a reused module. But none of the three verified capability defects were fixed. Section 7 still resolves lost alternate-screen output by asking the reviewer to reproduce its previous message 'verbatim' into a file — retrospective regeneration from possibly-compacted context, the same class of silent lossy substitution the task forbids — while the harness transcripts that Herdr's own agent_session pointer and the installed ~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh expose go unmentioned. Goal activation is still verified by scraping 'visible goal UI/status' on the Codex alternate screen, and I confirmed ~/.codex/goals_1.sqlite ships a migrated thread_goals table (objective, status active|paused|blocked|usage_limited|budget_limited|complete, token_budget, tokens_used, time_used_seconds, updated_at_ms) plus thread_goal_continuation_deferrals, which answers Q24 without any new artifact. The capability table still lacks the mandated Claude/Codex/OpenCode route axis, and every Paseo cell still reads 'Available' with no version and no inferred label though paseo is not installed. The successor rule still requires a confirmed lineId that no real catalog supplies. skills/adopt-project still receives no audit verdict. Additionally, its preference for send-keys with a separate Enter to enter /goal is contradicted by the installed skill, which states verbatim that 'agent prompt atomically submits text and encoded Enter while honoring the pane's live bracketed-paste mode' — so the chosen mechanism is more fragile than the one it rejects.

blocking_findings.description: Unchanged from the previous round: section 7's Herdr path asks the reviewer to write its previous message 'verbatim' to a Markdown file after the panel read fails. An LLM regenerates rather than retrieves its own prior output, and after compaction will paraphrase, compress and drop caveats — the same silent lossy substitution the task forbids, but harder to detect because it arrives as a file. Verified alternatives ignored: herdr agent get exposes agent_session (present in the API schema), the installed ~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh populates transcript pointers, and ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl plus ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl hold authoritative full transcripts. A prospective write-to-file instruction in the initial prompt is also strictly better than a retrospective re-export.
blocking_findings.required_change: Make retrieval prospective (worker writes its full verdict to a file as part of its task and returns only the path) and add reading the route's own transcript JSONL as the non-generative secondary path. Demote 'ask the agent to re-export' to last resort and label it explicitly as lossy regeneration rather than verbatim retrieval.

blocking_findings.description: Activation is still confirmed by reading 'visible goal UI/status' in the Codex TUI — the alternate screen the same document proves is unrecoverable — and section 23 consequently downgrades Herdr goal support to 'requires a disposable activation test; fallback applies until then'. ~/.codex/goals_1.sqlite contains migrated tables thread_goals (thread_id, goal_id, objective, status with six values including usage_limited/budget_limited, token_budget, tokens_used, time_used_seconds, updated_at_ms) and thread_goal_continuation_deferrals, providing queryable native confirmation with no new goal.json, FSM or proxy CLI. Row count is currently 0, so end-to-end behaviour still needs a live test, but the capability question is largely settled by the shipped migration.
blocking_findings.required_change: Verify and monitor goal state from the harness's own goal store rather than terminal scraping; remove the unnecessary fallback downgrade for Herdr+Codex; and note the store layout is a version-specific detail to re-probe, not a stable API.

blocking_findings.description: Section 4.2 of the task mandates analysis per backend AND per Claude/Codex/OpenCode route; the table still has only a backend axis, reporting 'Context fill: Unavailable на Herdr layer' and 'Last-turn time: Inferred' as the complete answer, although thread_goals supplies tokens_used, token_budget, time_used_seconds and updated_at_ms at the route layer. Separately, paseo is not installed (no version is cited for it, unlike Herdr and Omnigent) yet its cells read 'Available' for native status, full transcript and last-turn time, and the Omnigent 'export/history' transcript claim is stated without the confirming command.
blocking_findings.required_change: Add the route dimension and relabel every cell as available (naming the layer) | inferred (naming the source) | unavailable. Mark all Paseo cells inferred (docs only, CLI not installed) and cite omnigent session export explicitly. Re-derive the cache/compaction recommendation from the corrected table.

blocking_findings.area: model successor rule and helper justification
blocking_findings.description: The single surviving helper is what distinguishes architecture level 2 from level 1, but its successor rule still requires 'vendor и подтверждённый lineId' while ModelRef.lineId is optional and no derivation rule is given. On the real catalog (~/.codex/models_cache.json: gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-sol-wm, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini) nothing supplies lineId, so the rule needs an unpriced hand-maintained lineage map or degrades permanently to AMBIGUOUS_LINEAGE. The document also does not note that a native model catalog with fetched_at and etag already exists for the Codex route, weakening the multi-SDK discovery justification.
blocking_findings.required_change: Define a lineage rule derivable from actual catalog data (vendor plus family, with worked examples and explicit handling of same-release suffix variants), state why a local catalog snapshot is still needed, and acknowledge the existing native caches so the helper's scope is honestly bounded.

blocking_findings.area: goal input mechanism contradicted by installed skill
blocking_findings.description: Section 6 states 'предпочтителен key-level ввод с отдельным Enter' for /goal and treats agent prompt as unreliable for slash commands. The installed herdr --skill states verbatim: 'agent prompt atomically submits text and encoded Enter while honoring the pane's live bracketed-paste mode.' The rejected mechanism is the atomic one; send-keys with a separate Enter is the fragile one. The skill also documents that --wait tracks lifecycle state rather than turn boundaries, which the premature-idle logic depends on and which is not mentioned.
blocking_findings.required_change: Use agent prompt for goal submission per the installed skill, and require waiting for idle before prompting because --wait may be satisfied by completion of an already-active turn.

blocking_findings.description: skills/adopt-project still receives no keep/replace/delete/defer verdict in either audit table despite section 18 covering individual test fixtures. Separately, agent-required mo-e2e is specified to print AGENT_REQUIRED and exit 2 while mo-qc is the recommended aggregate, but the document never states whether mo-qc depends on mo-e2e — if it does, standard make semantics fail every QC run in agent-E2E projects, and the exit-2 sentinel has no named machine consumer even though manifests were deleted for exactly that reason.
blocking_findings.required_change: Add an explicit verdict for adopt-project, state that mo-qc must not depend on an agent-required mo-e2e, and either name the consumer of the exit-2 sentinel or drop it in favour of the agent reading full output.

assumptions: The absent paseo CLI reflects the real target environment, so all Paseo capability claims must be labelled inferred until probed.
Reading ~/.codex and ~/.claude state files read-only is an acceptable methodology mechanism, introducing no new artifact or protocol.
goals_1.sqlite and the rollout transcript layout are version-specific details a skill must re-probe rather than hardcode; I treat them as proof the capability exists, not as stable public APIs.
